newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom may buy share in KDD undersea cable.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom may buy share in KDD undersea cable.

text.p: Domestic telephone company Japan Telecom Co may buy capacity in an undersea cable to be laid by international carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co by mid-1999, a Japan Telecom official told Reuters.
"We are studying a plan to buy a minor share in the planned undersea cable," Japan Telecom director Taro Sasaki said in an interview.
"We don't need much. It would be just a tiny share (of transmission capacity)," he said without elaborating.
Japan Telecom, if it goes ahead, would be the second operator to lease part of the cable after DDI Corp.
DDI said in December it would buy a 20 percent share in the capacity of the 100 billion yen cable, which will loop around Japan's three main islands and carry 1.2 million telephone lines.
DDI relies on microwave transmission of voice and data and lacks optic fibre networks.

Japan Telecom's possible move is seen by some industry officials as an attempt to establish closer business ties with KDD, following liberalisation of the Japanese market and restructuring of the colossal Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
Japan Telecom owns extensive optic fibre networks throughout the country except on the southern island of Kyushu.
Other analysts said Japan Telecom may want to close gaps in its fibre optic network by using the underseas cable as it hopes to extend its business to international services shortly.
Japan Telecom president Koichi Sakata told a news conference recently that it would announce its international business plans in February.
